overview: From 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-06, ethereum-optimism/specs had 5 new PRs (0 merged), 1 new issues, and 15 active contributors.

topIssues.title: SDM: make it clear that violating refund(i) <= evmGasUsed(i) invalidates the entire block
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
If a sequencer actually broadcasts an invalid postexec tx, by trying to refund too much gas, verifiers will reject the entire block.

Not to be confused with sequencer policies / safeguards (it can prevent itself from doing the above by catching buggy policies on the fly).

topPRs.title: specs: make airgap delays configurable per chain
topPRs.author: zkfrov
topPRs.body:
## Context

The per-chain air gap (optimism-private#684) moves `PROOF_MATURITY_DELAY_SECONDS`,
`DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS` and the `DelayedWETH` delay from implementation
immutables to per-chain values set at initialization and adjustable by the L1 ProxyAdmin
owner within bounds. The specs still describe them as immutables.

## Changes

- `fault-proof/stage-one/optimism-portal.md`: proof maturity delay is per chain and read at
  check time. Finalization condition stated as
  `max(provenAt + proofMaturityDelay, resolvedAt + finalityDelay)`. Adds the bound getters,
  the setter and aOP-004 for portals sharing an `ETHLockbox`.
- `fault-proof/stage-one/anchor-state-registry.md`: same for the finality delay. Notes it is
  shared by every chain and game type using the registry.
- `experimental/contracts/dispute/delayed-weth.md`: same for the withdrawal delay. Also
  updates `initialize` and pause lookup to the `ETHLockbox` model.
- `protocol/configurability.md`: the three requirements become ranges with the L1 ProxyAdmin
  owner as administrator.
- `bridge-integration.md`, `bond-incentives.md`, `fault-dispute-game.md`, `zk-dispute-game.md`:
  cross-references updated.

Setter and getter names are provisional until optimism-private#686 and #692 open.

topPRs.title: lagoon: specify block-level warming as a producer policy with a net refund
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Why

The block-level warming policy rebates the gross EIP-2929 surcharge on block-warm accesses. The EIP-3529 refund cap (gas spent / 5) and the EIP-7623 calldata floor both depend on gas spent, so when either binds, part of that surcharge never reached the transaction's gas used:

- **Cap binds:** up to one fifth of the rebate is unbacked. In the audit's example, a transaction is charged 65,324 gas against 105,324 had its block-warm reads been priced transaction-warm.
- **Floor binds:** the whole rebate is unbacked.

These are internal audit findings SDM-M5 and SDM-L10. The spec's only wording on this, "rebate only accesses actually charged the cold price", supports both a gross and a net reading. It also left it unclear whether the policy is a consensus rule at all.

## What changes

- **Gas Refund Semantics** keeps only the consensus rule: clients apply the included refund, subject to the validity rules and `refund(i) <= evmGasUsed(i)`.
- **Refund Policy** (new subsection) states that a refund policy is not a consensus rule. Verifiers don't run it, and a block whose refunds differ from it is still valid.
- **Block-Level Warming Policy** (new subsection) has four parts:
  - *Warmth States:* defines cold, block-warm and transaction-warm, and what is warm from the start of a transaction.
  - *Surcharges:* the per-access amounts (2500 account, 2000 `SLOAD`, 2100 `SSTORE`) and which opcodes they cover.
  - *Refund Amount:* the policy refunds the **net saving**, `evmGasUsed(i) - warmGasUsed(i)`, where `warmGasUsed` recomputes the cap and floor with the surcharges removed. A refund therefore never charges a transaction less than it would have used had its block-warm accesses been priced transaction-warm.
  - *Known Limitations:* non-normative.
- **`evmGasUsed`** is now defined explicitly as after the EIP-3529 cap and the EIP-7623 floor.
- **Producer and Verifier** and **Security Considerations** now point to the policy subsection and repeat that it is guidance for producers.

There is no consensus change. Verifiers behave exactly as before.

Implementation: ethereum-optimism/optimism#23191

## Checks

`markdownlint-cli2`, `doctoc` and `cspell` all pass on `sdm.md`. Five opcode names were added to `words.txt`.

topPRs.title: lagoon: specify how subblock consumers apply the post-exec transaction
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a short clarification to [post-exec.md § Subblocks](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/main/specs/protocol/lagoon/post-exec.md#subblocks) on how consumers apply `diff.post_exec_tx`. This is the specs part of internal audit finding SDM-M2 (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#372).

The section already says that the in-progress block's post-exec transaction is carried in `diff`, never in `transactions`, and that it is provisional until the block is sealed. It does not say that the block a subblock describes *includes* that transaction. The op-reth flashblocks consumer read it that way: it executed `diff.transactions` alone, so its pending receipts and balances left out SDM refunds.

The new subsection, **"The in-progress block includes the latest post-exec transaction"**, follows the section's decision / rationale / consumer-implication format:
- **Normative:** the in-progress block's transaction list is the concatenation of `diff.transactions` so far, followed by the latest subblock's `diff.post_exec_tx` when present. Canonical gas, settlement and receipts follow from that list exactly as for a sealed block.
- **Consumer implication:**
  - A consumer that executes the in-progress block MUST execute that post-exec transaction last and apply its refunds as a verifier does.
  - Because the payload is provisional and the refund policy is sequencer-defined, a consumer that reuses earlier execution MUST apply refunds from the current `post_exec_tx`, not carry earlier ones forward.
  - Transaction-list comparisons with a sealed block (e.g. reorg detection) include the post-exec transaction.

No wire-format change and no change to any sealed-block rule.

Companion implementation: ethereum-optimism/optimism#23157.

## Checks

- `doctoc` TOC regenerated.
- `markdownlint-cli2` and `cspell` pass on the changed file.

topPRs.title: fault-proofs: require respected parents for respected ZK games
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Respected ZK games require parents that were respected when they were created, preventing a claim created while ZK was not respected from becoming the starting point for a withdrawal-eligible claim after a switch back. Games created while ZK is not respected may continue existing proposal chains.

Companion specification update for https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23208. Markdown lint, spelling, and table-of-contents checks pass.

topPRs.title: lagoon: add the 7702 delegate of tx.to to the intrinsic-warmth list
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
The refund-policy correctness note's intrinsic-warmth list omits the EIP-7702 delegation target of `tx.to`: revm resolves it warm and free of charge while EIP-2780 is inactive, so a transaction never pays a cold surcharge for it and the block-warming policy must not rebate a block-warm delegate.

Companion to the policy fix ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#333; both close audit finding **SDM-M4** (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#374). The spec gap was called out in the finding itself.
